decisions.rationale: Assistant Chat's shared-contract consumer boundary is adjacent to slash/chat and command owner-deference contracts, but those comparators govern different command and reconciliation lifecycles rather than the same Assistant Chat privacy, recovery, state, and failure boundary.

Browser ownership and stale-canon cleanup are relevant to rendering trust, but the comparator does not carry the same rendering-source authority, preview trust-tier lifecycle, product-surface outcome, or discovery-lineage failure boundary.

The Kubernetes comparators cover doctor degradation and deep-link session safety, which are members of or neighbors to project-focused Kubernetes scope; neither defines the same whole-scope authority, included/excluded operations, scale boundary, and failure semantics.

User-command ownership and blocked-action projection are related command authorities, but panel commands retain product-wide requested, blocked, and effective state semantics at a different command class and state boundary.

The identity-schema and actor-envelope comparators overlap actor, provider, account, and approval vocabulary, but each governs a different record, lifecycle, authorization boundary, and failure behavior from the opaque references in goal runtime events.

Reference-first browser evidence and general redaction oracles are relevant, but the anchor uniquely binds browser-session redaction manifests to GUI-automation artifact handling; the comparators have different artifact authorities, lifecycles, and enforcement failures.

The related items address untrusted paths, URLs, and artifact references in other contracts, but none shares this manifest locator schema, its consumers, containment boundary, or URL/path failure semantics.

Receipt ownership and fragmented privacy routing are plausible neighbors, but they govern different records and cross-owner seams; neither has the manifest producer, tenant/workspace owner, evidence audience, and responsible-consumer boundary.

DL-022 and the anchor describe the same blocked-episode approval-resolution lifecycle: identity and freshness binding, duplicate or concurrent decisions, single-use/replay handling, mismatch recovery, resumption, and durable failure visibility. Their details are complementary within one authority and state boundary.

General privacy routing and identity-record lifecycle are related, but approval provenance is a specific durable attribution record with its own minimization, access, support-export, and deletion outcomes; treating it as the umbrella identity lifecycle would collapse a member boundary.

The comparator contracts implement blocked-episode and routing members of the aggregate HITL authority/identity PlanUnit group. Umbrella/member structure is not merge equivalence, and their lifecycle and failure scopes are narrower.

The blocked-action projection contract overlaps surfaces and authority routing, but it does not cover the same HITL boundary-unification, compatibility, transition-report, tray-correlation, and bounded debug-grant lifecycle.

Domain approval classification is related to gate selection, but it does not define the mapping from phase/task/subtask toggles to package or seam gates, precedence among matching toggles, deduplication, or graph/group mismatch behavior.

DP-062 and the anchor govern the same durable approval-reuse authority through approval_scope_key plus actor, lane, run, and account context. Both cover reuse lifetime, revocation or drift, collision/isolation, downstream validity, and failure closure, so the privacy gaps are part of one lifecycle rather than a separate feature.

Restart recovery, blocked-action projection, and negative readiness predicates are constituent or consuming contracts of the aggregate HITL wait/recovery/permission group; their authority, lifecycle, and failure boundaries are narrower.

Approval snapshot lifetime, restart recovery, and readiness gating are adjacent, but none governs the same pending-approval timer, authoritative clock, expiry-versus-resolution race, exactly-once wake, and restart catch-up boundary.

Approval narrowing, domain target binding, and allowed-action execution are directly related, but they address authority limits or action invocation after selection rather than the typed permission-ladder-to-runtime-action composition and label mapping itself.

The related records own underlying approval, episode, and projection behavior. Ask-flow is a consumer label over those shared contracts, so merging it with an owner contract would erase a distinct consumer and state-machine boundary.

Decision-policy defaults and no-human conflicts are plausible neighbors, but they govern pre-execution ambiguity or contradictory trigger policies, while the anchor defines the bounded runtime classes that may seek user authority. The lifecycle and failure outcomes differ.

FileSafe security events and recovery readiness can block execution, but PAUSE.md is a separate file-backed precedence gate with creator, validation, expiry, exact-action exception, malformed-file, and race semantics.

Blocked-episode identity, routing, and approval replay are lifecycle neighbors, but HITLRequest is the interoperable request wire/state contract; the comparators do not share its request kinds, delivery, response, versioning, copy, and conformance boundary.

Visible operations, FileSafe overrides, and allowed-action IDs are relevant safety controls, but skip and abort are destructive runtime command payloads with distinct confirmation, transactional, compensation, result-event, and stale-run semantics.

Polling resilience, episode restart, and readiness are related recovery mechanics, but none supplies the same per-HITL-request-kind timeout action matrix, late/duplicate response handling, authority choice, expired presentation, and transition tests.

Setup/Health presentation, command diagnostics, and approval UX are plausible members of user-visible quality, but the anchor spans all HITL surfaces, redaction, accessibility, localization, offline/stale presentation, scale, support, and metrics. Umbrella/member overlap is not equivalence.

General identity-record privacy and runtime-context visibility are related, but the anchor is the interview-to-runtime handoff packet with consumer-specific disclosure and requested/effective account fields; storage, audience, and lifecycle boundaries differ.

Identity lifecycle and propagation supply source truth, while the anchor governs the user-visible summary projection and mandatory mismatch, label, redaction, accessibility, localization, and staleness indicators. Projection and source contracts are distinct.

Requested/effective identity schema, propagation, and account-switch invalidation are prerequisites, but prelaunch alignment is a fail-closed equality and integrity gate with a resolver and repair path at a different state transition.

The continuity contract mentions conflict handling, but it is a broad obligation set rather than the same durable unresolved-conflict record, competing-value provenance, authorized resolution, blocking scope, resume persistence, and audit transition.

The comparators define identity fields or actor envelopes that can populate a handoff, but the anchor is the closed, versioned interview handoff packet with referential consistency, signature/trust, replay, and validation-error semantics. These are dependencies, not equivalents.

Global untrusted-input routing and Free Models import authenticity are related trust controls, but provider-native interview imports have their own canonical-field precedence, path sanitization, schema validation, signature, quarantine, and error lifecycle.

Budget exhaustion and parallel-evidence capacity are adjacent resource constraints, but reviewer-cap reservation has its own atomic allocation, fairness, cancellation release, retry timing, and user-visible exhaustion outcome.

Compile/runtime boundaries and buildability policy support the summary-only posture, but the anchor is a document-authority and labeling contradiction. The comparators govern executable eligibility and closure states, not the same title/summary contract.

The auth carry-through comparator and anchor describe the same provider-auth reconciliation lifecycle across storage, runtime, and UI, including active versus retired provider routes, requested/effective truth, revocation, offline or unavailable states, stale labels, and mismatch failure. The anchor adds adverse-state oracle detail within that same authority.

Owner-map precedence, package-overseer scope, and cross-cutting ownership are related governance boundaries, but none defines the same package-local to seam-level authority handoff, trigger, conflict precedence, partial-failure owner, and consuming-surface lifecycle.

The account-switch comparator and anchor govern the same requested/effective multi-account switch lifecycle: account-sensitive state invalidation or partitioning, queued-work reauthorization, switch history, and adverse failure handling. The anchor identifies missing transaction, concurrency, privacy, and acceptance details within that same boundary.

External-adapter bounds and subsystem owner splits support native ownership, but they do not define the workbench's typed service interfaces, trust and error taxonomy, cancellation, or degraded behavior when the remote control plane or interop is lost.

Non-authoritative history projections and restart history are related, but the anchor concerns the specific lineage predicate that decides when a historical run is treated as superseded, including writer authority, transition, and recovery oracle.

Browser ownership, reference-first evidence, and research-safe policy are relevant, but agent-driven preview has a distinct navigation-permission, untrusted-content, credential, destructive-action, network-loss, capture-redaction, and evidence-validity lifecycle.

The web-provider consumer map and generic domain-approval binding are related, but they do not enumerate or validate the six web operations, native batch invariants, approval stages, transition authority, denial behavior, or cross-owner oracle.

DockerHub authentication, API/CLI ownership, side-effect approvals, and operation lifecycle are members of registry management. The anchor is the bounded parity umbrella, so merging any member would conflate scope and preserve neither identical lifecycle nor failure semantics.

The command catalog lifecycle also has merge and update concerns, but it is a different catalog authority and user outcome from the code-shipped GUI tool base plus settings overlay keyed by stable framework/tool IDs.

Host blockers, provider recovery evidence, and availability enums are plausible neighbors, but MCP selection owns per-provider enablement and adapter degradation across partial availability, auth loss, changed tool identity, denial, and runtime failure.

Shared-route shape, serialization trust, and route ownership are directly related, but the anchor is the operational-target identity invariant that forbids view state from becoming authority. Wire shape, restore safety, and owner declarations have different failure boundaries.

Provider binary identity and doctor degradation are related checks, but this anchor specifically requires executing a selected custom tool and validating its evidence under timeout, sandbox, exit, side-effect, and canonical-evidence oracles.

General privacy routing, certification evidence, and debug evidence have similar lifecycle dimensions, but GUI media and manifest-linked artifacts have different capture, rendering, consent, capacity, access, export, and accessible-presentation boundaries.

Profile isolation, browser ownership, and reference-first evidence are related controls, but attaching to an already-open browser creates a distinct live profile/tab authorization, cookie/storage exposure, unrelated-tab exclusion, reauthorization, and detach-cleanup lifecycle.

Normalized host blockers, safe doctor degradation, and negative readiness predicates are relevant, but auto mode owns backend selection and must classify visible-preflight failures into safe availability fallback versus trust, permission, integrity, version, or target-identity blocks.

Debug overlay authority, browser ownership, and auth-family isolation are adjacent, but the anchor is the browser-debug trust boundary: ephemeral session default, attention_required instead of unrelated authenticated reuse, and declared-host preflight.

Privacy routing, debug evidence lifecycle, and research-safe policy are relevant, but mobile capture owns device permissions, personal-data reset/isolation, simulator or device disconnect, degraded network, localization/accessibility matrices, and artifact cleanup.

Buildx preflight separation and distinct side-effect approvals help interpret action scope, but neither is the same contradictory Compose prerequisite governing local build and publish entry points. The authoritative conflict remains a separate spec-state defect.

CRAU-085 and the anchor describe the same Docker publish and Unraid result-state lifecycle, including the closed status enum, needs_review exits, transition authority, retries or resume, cancellation and timeout races, duplicate review, and partial-commit recovery. These are complementary details within one operation-state boundary.
